drugRefs.why: Covers the major invasive bacterial dysentery pathogens (Shigella, Campylobacter, invasive E. coli) and shortens illness duration and carriage in confirmed bacterial dysentery.

drugRefs.coverage: Preferred alternative given rising fluoroquinolone resistance in Shigella and Campylobacter in many regions, and useful in pediatric and pregnant patients where fluoroquinolones are avoided.
Used for severe disease requiring hospitalization or when oral therapy is not tolerated.

coverageMatrix.completeness: Either agent covers the majority of dysentery pathogens; local resistance data should guide final choice.
gaps: Entamoeba histolytica is not covered by either agent — requires metronidazole/tinidazole if confirmed on stool microscopy.

stewardship.deescalation: If stool culture identifies Entamoeba histolytica, discontinue antibacterial agents and switch to metronidazole/tinidazole. If a specific bacterial organism with known susceptibility is identified, narrow to the most targeted oral agent.

framework: Avoid antimotility agents (e.g., loperamide) in dysentery as they may prolong invasive infection and increase complication risk (e.g., toxic megacolon, HUS with EHEC).
Send stool culture before or concurrent with starting antibiotics whenever feasible to allow de-escalation/confirmation.
Reserve empiric ciprofloxacin only where local Shigella/Campylobacter resistance rates are acceptable; otherwise azithromycin is preferred first-line.
